title: Service credit allocator and commitment sculptor for SLO programs
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Problem: Teams currently commit to SLO improvements and mitigation work as discrete initiatives, but we lack a consistent way to (a) allocate portions of a service's error budget to specific initiatives, (b) amortize reliability work across cycles, and (c) reconcile actual burn vs committed credits when incidents occur. This creates ambiguity for prioritization and inconsistent cross-team incentives.

Proposed solution: Build a 'Service Credit Allocator' and 'Commitment Sculptor' flow in the Console and the initiatives ledger. Features include:
- Per-initiative credit allocation: PMs can assign a percent of a service's monthly error budget to an initiative (e.g., canary rollout, infra refactor).
- Amortization schedules: credits may be applied upfront, spread evenly across cycles, or gated to deployment windows.
- Automated reconciliation: when SLI incidents consume budget, the system attributes burn to active allocations and surfaces delta to owners.
- Cross-team transfer & dispute flow: short-lived credit transfers with approval workflow.
- Exportable ledger and visualizations: per-service timeline showing committed credits, actual burn, and carry-forward adjustments.

Trade-offs considered: Keep the first iteration lightweight: no automatic enforcement (no auto-throttling), focus on visibility and reconciliation. Complex enforcement rules (auto-repricing, SLA penalties) deferred to later phases. Aim for strong auditability and a clear manual override path.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: ability to create/edit a per-initiative credit allocation with schedule options (upfront, even, gated)
Backend: ledger model persisted for credits and reconciliations with at least monthly granularity
Recon job: nightly attribution job that maps incident SLI burn to active allocations and writes reconciliation events
Notifications: owners receive a reconciliation summary when their initiative's credited balance drops below threshold
Exports: CSV of ledger entries and a time-series view in the reliability dashboard
updates: 2026-02-11 — Discovery complete. Spent a week interviewing three service owners and oncall leads; common need is visibility and a single source of truth for committed credits.

2026-02-13 — Architecture spike with ENG: landed on a ledger table (service_id, initiative_key, allocation_pct, schedule_type, start_cycle, end_cycle) and a nightly attribution job that joins incidents to active allocations. PR outline drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821

2026-02-15 — UX draft reviewed by Design (Maya Singh). Feedback: add a lightweight dispute/transfer modal; prefer calendar-based gating for schedules. Updated mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF_ui_mock
2026-02-18 — Security review checklist started; no KMS changes required for initial telemetry, flagging for later data-retention discussion.
2026-02-20 — Roadmapped to console-2026.04. Eng capacity requested: 2 backend sprints + 1 UX sprint. Budgeting sync scheduled with GTM on 2026-02-25.
